intro: We hold a recorded main-programme fee of up to ₹{{budget}} lakh for {{count}} published B.Tech / B.E. colleges in India. This list is for students looking at the best B.Tech / B.E. colleges under ₹1 lakh, and it needs a careful reading of each card.
Ranked colleges that fit the budget come first, then the rest are ordered by recorded total fee, lowest first. A low figure can be one-year tuition, so do not treat every card as a four-year cost.
listLead: The first cards include SV University College of Engineering in Tirupati, Government Engineering College Thrissur, and NIT Hamirpur. The NIT Hamirpur card shows ₹15,000 for B.Tech Civil, which should be checked on the official fee notice.
snapshot: Across the {{feeN}} published colleges here, the median recorded fee is {{feeMedian}}. The middle half sits between {{feeP25}} and {{feeP75}}.

Most listings are private ({{private}}), with {{public}} public institutes. Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Andhra Pradesh have the most colleges on this budget list.
JEE Main is the exam most often linked here, followed by TNEA and other state tests. Use the list of top B.Tech / B.E. colleges in India 2026 as a shortlist, then confirm the official fee notice.
firstCollegesLead: SV University College of Engineering shows a recorded CSE fee of ₹10,800–₹17,350, and GECT Thrissur shows ₹11,610–₹13,350, both with 2023 placement figures in our records. Confirm whether those fees are one year or the full four-year programme.

NIT Hamirpur’s Civil Engineering card at ₹15,000 is almost certainly not the complete B.Tech cost, and the branch on the card is Civil, not Computer Science. Some later private-college fees also look like a single-year figure.

sections.heading: How to read an engineering fee under ₹1 lakh
paragraphs: Public-college tuition is often published by year or semester, plus hostel and mess charges separately. A card under ₹1 lakh may therefore be one academic year, especially at an NIT or a state university.
Fees under ₹10,000 are treated as data errors and are not quoted as a minimum. Always open the official fee notice before you budget for four years.

compare.heading: How to compare the best B.Tech / B.E. colleges under ₹1 lakh
paragraphs: Start with the branch and the fee notice, not only the number on the card.
Then check these points on the official site:
bullets: Whether the fee is for one year or the full programme, and whether hostel, mess and institute fees are included.
The branch on the card, because a Civil Engineering fee is not a substitute for the Computer Science fee at the same campus.
The entrance route (JEE Main, TNEA, or another state CET) and the cut-off for your category.
The latest official placement report for that branch, with the year clearly stated.

faqs.question: How many engineering colleges here have a fee under ₹1 lakh?
faqs.answer: {{count}} published B.Tech / B.E. colleges in our records have a main-programme fee of up to ₹{{budget}} lakh, and colleges without a recorded fee do not appear on this budget list.

faqs.question: Is the NIT Hamirpur fee of ₹15,000 for the full B.Tech?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not, because official NIT charges are usually published by semester or year, so treat ₹15,000 as a figure to verify on the institute fee notice, not as a four-year total.

faqs.question: What is the typical fee on this under-₹1-lakh list?
faqs.answer: Among the {{feeN}} published colleges here, the median recorded fee is {{feeMedian}}, and the middle half falls between {{feeP25}} and {{feeP75}}.

faqs.question: Why are IITs not on this under-₹1-lakh list?
faqs.answer: The IIT fees we hold are above ₹1 lakh, so those campuses appear on the wider engineering fee list and on the under-₹5-lakh list instead.

faqs.question: Are these low fees always for the full four-year programme?
faqs.answer: Not always, because some public-college figures look like one-year tuition, so confirm the official fee notice before you shortlist a college on price alone.
